turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Price section didn't work. Too many numbers at too many sizes. Couldn't spot the total without reading every label."

We want to understand what you meant by "couldn't spot the total without reading every label", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The Total row sits at the bottom of the summary card with no visual separation from the Subtotal and Shipping rows above it, so it doesn't stand out as the final figure.

B) The Total label appears in bold but its corresponding value ($288.99) is displayed at the same size as the Subtotal figure directly above it, making the two amounts equally prominent in the layout.

C) The Order Summary section has no dedicated area or boundary that isolates the Total row — it shares the same card space as the individual line items, so the eye has no structural anchor to land on first.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What kind of work situation typically brings you to a screen showing order totals like this?
turns.a: Team purchase. External deadline. I'm the one confirming the amount — others depending on it being right. No time to hunt through a price breakdown.

turns.q: When you looked at the section showing those amounts, what specific figure were you trying to confirm was correct before signing off for your team?
turns.a: Confirm the total. First look. No hunting.

turns.q: If the total figure were visually distinct from the subtotal in this layout, what would tell you at a glance that you'd found the number you needed to confirm?
turns.a: Total clearly the most prominent number — obviously larger than everything else. No ambiguity about which number it is. That's the success state.

turns.q: When you look at the total amount compared to the subtotal directly above it — is it the size of the number itself that makes them feel equally weighted, or is it something about the color or heaviness of the text?
turns.a: Five type sizes in one small section — 8px, 10px, 11px, 20px, 22px — no deliberate scale. Total isn't clearly dominant. Can't scan it — size isn't carrying the hierarchy signal. Barrier: size mix with no step means every number competes and reading labels is required. Fix: reduce to three deliberate sizes. Total at 18–20px — the dominant number. Line items all 13–14px — consistent, reads as a group. Secondary labels ≤11px — clearly subordinate. If those three steps were in place, the total would be findable at a glance. Right now it isn't. That's the barrier and the fix.
